2026-11-14.title: Saturday of the Thirty-second Week in Ordinary Time
readings: We ought to support such people, so that we may become co-workers with the truth
Blessed the man who fears the Lord
Pray always and do not lose heart
2026-11-14.alt: Optional: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2026-11-14.verse: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray always and not to lose heart.
theo: Luke tells us the point before the parable: we need “to pray always and not to lose heart”. A widow, the most powerless person in that society, keeps coming to an unjust judge until he gives in just to be rid of her. If even such a judge yields to persistence, how much more will God, who is not unjust but a loving Father, “grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night”? Then the haunting question: “when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?”

The Third Letter of John praises Gaius for welcoming travelling missionaries, “even though they are strangers to you”. By supporting them, he says, “we may become co-workers with the truth”. Persistent prayer and generous hospitality go together: those who pray for the Kingdom also open their homes and purses to those who spread it.
outline: Ask: what have you stopped praying for because the answer was slow?
Persistence is not nagging God; it is trusting him.
He is not the unjust judge; he is our Father.
Support those who spread the Gospel.
live: Take up again a prayer you abandoned and pray it every day this week.
Give to the missions or help a visiting priest or sister.
2026-11-14.prayer: Lord, teach me to pray always and not to lose heart. Strengthen my faith while I wait for your answer, and make me a co-worker with the truth, generous to those who proclaim your Gospel. Amen.

2026-11-14.question: Will the Lord find faith in me when he comes?

homily: Dear friends, Luke tells us the point before the parable: we need to pray always and not to lose heart (Luke 18:1). A widow, the most powerless person in that society, keeps coming to an unjust judge until he gives her justice just to be rid of her.

If even such a judge gives in to persistence, how much more will God, who is not unjust but a loving Father, grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night (Luke 18:7)? God is not reluctant. But persistent prayer changes us: it keeps our hope alive and our hearts turned to him.

Then Jesus asks a haunting question: when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth (Luke 18:8)? Faith is not only believing once; it is continuing to pray when the answer is slow. St John, in his third letter, praises Gaius for supporting the missionaries and so becoming a co-worker with the truth (3 John 8).
Choose one intention today, for a person, a healing, a reconciliation, and pray for it every day until Advent begins. Do not lose heart. The Father hears. Amen.
kids: Children, the widow kept asking and never gave up. Choose one person to pray for every day this month, and keep going!

intro: Persistent prayer, trust in a just Father, and generosity to those who spread the Gospel.

sub: Others can help hold up our arms.
q: Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed. But Moses' hands grew weary; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.
Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray always and not to lose heart.
points.apply: Take up again a prayer you abandoned.

sub: The judge was unjust; God is not.
The cry of the poor reaches him.
The real question is our faith.
q: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds, and it will not rest until it reaches its goal.

And will not God grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night? Will he delay long in helping them? I tell you, he will quickly grant justice to them. And yet, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?
points.apply: Pray today for someone suffering injustice.

sub: Gaius welcomed strangers sent by the Church.
We share in the work we support.
q: He said, “My lord, if I find favor with you, do not pass by your servant.”
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Give to the missions this week.

concl: Let him find faith in us.
